## math.averages — smoothers, rolling windows and running statistics

Does: Streaming averages and statistics: feed one value at a time with Update, read Value once IsReady.
Needs: Nothing. Construct with the period, keep the instance, call Update per value.

Types:
- `IEstimator` — What every streaming estimator in this namespace has in common: a current value, and whether it means anything yet. · `Value` · `IsReady` · `Reset()`
- `new Ema(int period)` — Exponential moving average, seeded with its first sample. · `IEstimator` · `Period` · `Count` · `Update(double sample)`
- `new Sma(int period)` — Simple moving average over a fixed window. · `IEstimator` · `Period` · `Count` · `Update(double sample)`
- `new Wilder(int period)` — Wilder's smoothing — `α = 1/period`, not `2/(period+1)`. · `IEstimator` · `Period` · `Count` · `Update(double sample)`
- `new Dema(int period)` — A double exponential smoother, so a fast average can be de-lagged without shortening its period. · `IEstimator` · `Period` · `Update(double sample)`
- `new EwmaVariance(double lambda = 0.94)` — Exponentially weighted mean and variance — Welford's statistic for a series whose distribution moves. · `IEstimator` · `Lambda` · `Mean` · `Variance` · `StandardDeviation` · `Update(double sample)` · `ZScoreOf(double value)`
- `new Welford()` — Welford's running mean and variance — the whole history, in constant space and one pass. · `IEstimator` · `Count` · `Mean` · `Variance` · `StandardDeviation` · `Update(double sample)` · `ZScoreOf(double value)`
- `new ZScore(int period, int minimumSamples = 0)` — A windowed z-score with an explicit warm-up, because the number is worthless before it converges. · `IEstimator` · `Period` · `MinimumSamples` · `Mean` · `StandardDeviation` · `Update(double sample)`
- `new RollingWindow(int capacity)` — A fixed-capacity ring of the most recent samples, with its statistics computed on demand. · `Capacity` · `Count` · `IsFull` · `Newest` · `Oldest` · `Item` · `Sum` · `Mean` · `Variance` · `StandardDeviation` · `Minimum` · `Maximum` · `Range` · `Update(double sample)` · `PositionOf(double value)` · `ZScoreOf(double value)` · `Quantile(double fraction)` · `Median()` · `Reset()`
- `Num` — The arithmetic guards every estimator in this namespace uses, exposed because authored code needs them too.
  - `double SafeDiv(double numerator, double denominator, double fallback = 0)` — `numerator` ÷ `denominator`, returning `fallback` when the denominator is zero, sub-epsilon, or not finite.
  - `double Finite(double value, double fallback = 0)` — `value` when it is finite, else `fallback`.
  - `double Clamp(double value, double minimum, double maximum)` — Constrains a value to a range.
  - `double ZScore(double value, double mean, double standardDeviation)` — How many standard deviations `value` sits from the mean, with the denominator floored.
  - `double LogReturn(double price, double previousPrice)` — The log return between two prices, or zero when either is non-positive.
  - `double Lerp(double from, double to, double t)` — Linear interpolation, with `t` clamped to [0, 1].
  - `double RoundToTick(double price, double tickSize)` — `price` snapped to the nearest multiple of `tickSize`.

Limits: O(1) per update. Value is meaningless until IsReady. Reset() to start over; do not re-feed values it has already seen.
